title: Researcher Analysis Toolkit for integrated and traceable evaluation of electrochemical, photoelectrochemical, and spectroscopic data
content: Electrochemical and photoelectrochemical data are often processed using several stand-alone programs, making it difficult to maintain a consistent workflow from raw data to reported results. Here, we introduce the Researcher Analysis Toolkit, a modular desktop application that brings together voltammetry, Tafel analysis, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), semiconductor and photoelectrochemical calculations, time-resolved photoluminescence fitting, optical band-gap estimation, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis. For EIS, the toolkit supports both user-defined circuit fitting and hierarchical screening of candidate circuits. The fitting workflow includes Lin–KK consistency testing, residual analysis, parameter-bound warnings, and approximate uncertainty and parameter-correlation diagnostics. Users retain control over fitting ranges and analysis settings, whereas calculations and data export follow a common workflow across modules. The software generates processed datasets, figures, tables, and analysis reports. Its operation is illustrated using representative module outputs, predefined synthetic EIS benchmarks, and experimental impedance data from an indium tin oxide (ITO) electrode coated with a cerium oxide-based composite. The integrated workflow is designed to simplify data handling and support documentation of analysis settings and outputs.
